notes:
Account overview: Twill Gate is building a latency-sensitive AI assistant for institutional traders. Primary goal is predictable latency under load and a firm throughput commitment for market hours. They skew strongly toward private/VPC deployment and require strict audit trails + KMS.

Key technical requirements (from SE calls):
- Throughput guarantee: baseline 900 req/min sustained for 9-5 ET trading window (avg 128 tokens per request); peak burst 2500 req/min for 10-minute spikes.
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile <= 220ms for <512-token responses, P50 target <= 70ms. Measurement: per-route p95 measured at the Redwood Console (tokenized).
- Reserved GPU planning: initial reserved pool of 8 H100-equivalent GPUs (customer prefers H100 sizing). Autoscale headroom + burst pool: +30% capacity allowed for 5-minute bursts with throttled billing.
- Model routing/fallback: primary pinned model (redwood-ver1-xxq); fallback to smaller quantized variant when capacity constrained. Need automatic billing adjustment when fallback invoked.

SLA negotiation specifics requested by customer/legal:
- Uptime target: negotiating between 99.95% and 99.99% for dedicated capacity. Twill prefers 99.99% for market-critical windows (08:30-16:00 ET).
- Credit schedule proposal under review: tiered credits, e.g. 99.95-99.99 -> 10% of monthly dedicated fee per 0.01% below SLO, 99.9-99.95 -> 20% per 0.01% below, cap 100% credits over consecutive breaches. Twill pushing for lower caps and financial cap = 3x monthly fee; legal wants operational remedies as well (hot-swap priority, capacity remediation timelines).
- Maintenance windows: prefer scheduled maintenance outside 06:00-19:00 ET; Redwood proposed monthly 2-hour maintenance with 72h notice and emergency patches with 8h notice. Twill asking for no forced maintenance during market hours or explicit opt-out for market-window days.
- Support & response times: P1 (production outage impacting market orders) — 15 min acknowledgement, 1 hour remediation SLA; P2 (significant impact) — 1 hour acknowledgement, 4 hour remediation; P3 — 4 hour acknowledgement, 24–72 hour remediation. Twill requests a named escalation path and weekly status updates for P1 incidents.
- Operational metrics & evidence: Twill requires token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-route traces for 90 days. Also wants audit log exports to their SIEM (Splunk) and monthly performance reviews.

Sticking points: legal wants clearer language on "fallback" behavior (billing, performance expectations). Security needs proof-of-concept for KMS integration (bring-your-own-key). Procurement needs final ARR before signing; finance wants the credit schedule capped.

Quotes from customer: "We need predictable latency when markets open — even short degradations cost us materially. Credits are fine, but remediation and prioritized capacity matter more."

Attached artifacts referenced in timeline and by legal: pricing deck, sample SLA template, draft MSA redlines, KMS integration guide.
